then.text: The Bruce is at rest, and so am I. Come and visit when you like. His heart, I mean. Mine's fine.

You faced the Black Douglas and survived? Then you know the story as well as anyone does. Take this: a pin in the shape of a crowned heart, like the one on the plaque. May it guard you from the blows that brawn hits you with.
Have you found the pig on the roof? Then speak to the knight in the corner. He doesn't bite, mostly. He plays the Black Douglas. Be firm with him.

else.text: Welcome to Melrose Abbey. It was a great Cistercian house until the English wrecked it, three times over. We've kept the best bits and, in the chapter house, something very special.

Robert the Bruce died in 1329 and asked that his heart be carried on crusade. His friend, Sir James Douglas, set out with it in a silver casket, and was killed in Spain in 1330. The heart was brought home and buried here at Melrose.

A lead casket was found in 1921, and found again in 1996, and the heart was reburied here in 1998 under a stone in the chapter house. Would you help me with a task? Find the pig on the roof outside, the one with the bagpipes. Then have a word with the Douglas man in the corner.

then.text: Splendid. The pig's outside, to the east of the abbey. You can't miss him. He's very loud.

else.text: No bother. He's been up there for centuries. He can wait.

then.text: A fair fight. Tell them the Douglas would have gone to Spain anyway. It was the heart that insisted.

So you've found the pig. Then you know the heart's here, and that I carried it. Tradition says that at Teba, outnumbered, I threw the casket ahead of me and cried: 'Lead on, as thou wert wont, and I will follow thee or die.'
Well. That's me answered. The Bruce would have been proud. I rather think his heart was.

else.text: Find the pig on the roof first. Then we'll talk about hearts. I'm a re-enactor, but I take it seriously.
Sir James Douglas, they called the Black Douglas, because he was dark, and because the English used his name to frighten their children. I'm only the re-enactor.
